title: The client sends a serialized description of what the server should do, and the server binds it to types and calls
index_line: T-0062 · CODE_EXEC · the RSC payload names modules and arguments; the decoder resolves and invokes them · node/javascript · corroborated
invariant_violated: A component wire format is treated as a data channel: the server framework wrote the encoder, so the decoder is trusted to read whatever it wrote. But the format carries *references* — module names, property paths, argument lists — and a decoder that resolves them faithfully lets the client describe an invocation rather than supply a value.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated request posts a serialized payload to a server-function endpoint (or to any route the RSC runtime decodes)
the decoder parses the payload into the framework's internal representation, including module references and argument lists
references are resolved against the server's module graph and materialised as callable values
the decoded structure points at a function the attacker chose, with arguments the attacker chose
the runtime invokes it while finishing hydration, before any authorization is applied to the described action
the invoked chain reaches a process-spawning primitive

source.http.body.value: the multipart/JSON RSC payload — a serialized graph, not a form; every field is a reference

sink.deser.native.value: the framework's payload decoder, which resolves module and property references into live objects

guard.none.value: no allow-list of resolvable references, and the endpoint is unauthenticated by design (it serves the public page)

encoding.object-stream.value: the payload's own serialization syntax: reference markers, property paths, argument tuples

preconditions.expr: the app uses a framework or bundler that ships the vulnerable RSC packages
the resolved react-server-dom-* version is in the affected range
an RSC-capable route is internet-reachable (a page render is enough)

success: a crafted payload produces a response containing the output of a server-side primitive
the effect appears even on routes with no server functions, when the app merely uses RSC
the request is a single POST with no credentials and no prior session
failure_like: the framework build includes the validation fix, or the app has no server-side React at all
false_positive: a generic 500 from a malformed payload — check whether the decoder ran before failing
a client-only React app: no server decode happens, so nothing to reach

hazards: any client-server wire format that carries references rather than values has this shape; treat the decoder as an RPC surface
the endpoint is public by design, so there is no auth boundary to hide behind
the practical check is a version check plus one probe on a page route with an RSC header — cheap, do it first
distinct from T-0007 (a blob naming types in a language deserializer) and T-0026 (a validator executing code): here the *protocol* is the gadget surface
non_transfers: frameworks whose wire format carries only values, with references resolved server-side
deployments pinned to fixed react-server-dom-* versions

provenance.author: React team security advisory, CVE-2025-55182
provenance.corroborates: the flaw in how React decodes payloads sent to React Server Function endpoints, the affected packages, and that RSC-only apps are also vulnerable

provenance.author: oss-security (Openwall mailing list)
provenance.corroborates: public disclosure thread with independent analysis
